preview: Software Developer interview experience at BNY Mellon for the 2023 FTE role detailing the online assessment, two technical rounds, and an HR round.
content: Software Developer Interview Experience VISHAL PATIL | B.Tech Electrical 2019 - 2023 For 2023 FTE (On-campus) 9th August 2022 BNY Mellon visited our campus for the FTE opportunity for Final Year students for Software Developer role. Around 200+ students had applied. Eligibility: No CGPA Criteria Branches Allowed: CS, IT, ExTC, Electronics, Electrical, and Mechanical. Round 1 - Online Assessment (6th August 2022) Online Test conducted on Hackerrank Platform having 4 DSA Questions to be completed within 90 Minutes. 1. Easy (50 Marks) - A variation of https://leetcode.com/problems/find-k-closest-elements/. All test cases passed. 2. Medium I (75 Marks) - Can’t recall the question but I was able to solve this completely. 3. Medium II (75 Marks) - Although it was a medium question but was harder than the hard question. I was able to only pass 5 test cases out of 15. 4. Hard (100 Marks) - A variation of Fractional Knapsack. I solved this partially using brute force passing 10 test cases out of 14. 21 students were Shortlisted for the Interviews. Technical Round 1 (60 Minutes Codepair Round on Hackerrank) 1. This round started with the famous “Tell me about yourself?” (PS. Try to add information that isn't on your resume, and please stay technical) 2. Then the interviewer asked me the language I’m familiar with. My answer was C++. Then questions were asked on C++. 3. What are insertion and extraction operators? 4. How can we take a string having spaces as input in c++? 5. How can we take a paragraph as input in c++ in a string? 6. Difference between pass by value and pass by reference? 7. What is a Data Structure? After this, the interviewer moved on to some OOPs questions 8. What do you understand by Object Oriented Programming? 9. What are a class and object? What is the difference between a class and an object? 10. What are the 4 pillars of Object Oriented Programming? 11. What is the difference between runtime and compile time polymorphism? (PS. This was asked as a cross question as I mentioned it in polymorphism) 12. Given a situation where you want to do pre-computation automatically on an object created from a class. What functionality of OOPs would you use to achieve the following task? (PS. The answer was a constructor. Some cross questions on constructors and destructors were asked) 13. What do you understand by deep copy and shallow copy? 14. What is the Diamond Problem and what is the solution for it? 15. What are foreign keys and primary keys? 16. ACID Properties in DBMS. I was then asked to join the codepair to solve the DSA questions. 17. The first DSA question was a tough one. I don’t exactly remember the question but to solve it completely one needed to do it using Trie Data Structure. I tried doing it using Brute force and was able to get 6/13 test cases passed. 18. The second DSA question was an easy one, where given a Linked List having the data as bits of a binary number. We had to return the Decimal form of the Binary Number. I was able to give the brute force in 5-7 minutes and also coded the optimized solution quickly and the interviewer seemed satisfied. 19. Lastly, the interviewer asked if I had any questions. (PS. Always ask 1-2 questions that show that you’re interested in the company as well as you get to know about the company and the work they do and their tech stack) 14 students were Shortlisted for Technical Round II. Technical Round 2 (75 Minutes Codepair Round on Hackerrank) 1. This round too started with the famous “Tell me about yourself?” 2. Then I was given a DSA question to solve on the Code Pair. The question was a variation of the Fractional Knapsack. I was able to solve this partially. After the DSA question, the interviewer asked me if I had any knowledge of system design or low-level design. I told her that I had knowledge about low-level Design but haven’t yet worked with system design. 3. Design a Parking system for the BNY office in Pune. The parking system should show you the remaining parking slots as well as who occupied which slot. There was a discussion of around 30-40 minutes on this question. I was confident after answering this as the interviewer looked a lot satisfied knowing the fact that I wasn’t able to solve the DSA Questions completely. Then I was asked questions regarding my Internship at PwC India and Centrestage. I was also asked about my Open Source Contributions and there was a discussion about the open-source and closed-source codebase. (PS. I thank all my learnings at neoG Camp for questions based on HTML, JavaScript, and React) 4. How can we pass data using an HTML attribute? 5. How can we run JS code in an HTML file? 6. What would be the result of 5+3+”7”? How do you solve this issue? 7. Hoisting in JavaScript. 8. What is React? What is the difference between React and Angular? 9. What is a state in React? 10. What do you understand by reconciliation? 11. Which one is better according to you Redux or ContextAPI and why? (PS. This question was asked because I had Redux as well as ContextAPI in my resume) 12. Lastly, the interviewer asked if I had any questions. 8 students were Shortlisted for the Final Round initially. Although 4 more were shortlisted by the End of the Day. HR Round (30 Minutes) 1. There were 2 interviewers who were quite chill in this round. They made me comfortable by asking questions like what I had for dinner. How was my day? How is the weather in Mumbai? How do I feel right now? 2. Tell me about yourself. 3. Tell me something about your family. 4. What did your day look like while interning at PwC India? 5. What were the challenges you faced during your internship at PwC India? How did you overcome those? 6. Tell me one learning from each of your past experiences. 7. Tell me about the positions of responsibilities you hold currently. What are the major challenges there? How do they differ from the Corporate Challenges? 8. Given a situation where you organized an event and some other club too organizes the event at the same time. How would you deal with this event knowing the fact that your audience would be divided in this scenario? 9. Why BNY? (PS. Always prepare for these questions beforehand. Try to match the company values and work along with your personality.) 10. Do you have any questions for us? Lastly before exiting one of the interviewer said “See you soon at BNY. Congratulations.” I was certain that I had been selected but had to wait for the official confirmation. The results were out the next day at 12:06 am. I was one among the 9 of the selected candidates🙃 Tips 1. Don’t fake yourself. Keep it original. 2. Make sure you enter with a smile and greet them because your first impression can have a lot of impacts. 3. Stay calm, confident, and clear while speaking. 4. Don’t lie about anything in your resume. If they caught you then you’re done. 5. Prepare the “Tell me about yourself” and a few common HR questions beforehand. 6. Always ask questions at the end. It shows that you are interested in that company. 7. If you finish your answer and the interviewer is silent ask politely whether he wants you to expand it further. 8. Keep a water bottle, a pen and paper, and extra headphones handy because anything can go wrong at any point and you should not regret not having a backup ready. 9. Don’t lose hope in rejection. Your rejections should make you strong. Resources (That I followed) ● DSA: Arsh Goyal SDE Sheet, Striver SDE Sheet ● OOPs: OOPs Roadmap - Love Babbar, InterviewBit OOPs FAQ ● DBMS: DBMS RoadMap - Love Babbar, InterviewBit DBMS FAQ ● OS: OS Roadmap - Love Babbar, InterviewBit OS FAQ ● SQL: Hackerrank SQL, W3School SQL Exercises ● Aptitude: Indiabix, Prepinsta ● Puzzles: GFG Puzzles “Believe in the process of Preparation and Hard work, Results will follow!” ALL THE BEST👍 PS. For any help, you can connect with me here.
